tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
# Rig card — VTI

*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
read-only on the repo.*

## Identity
- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert (closed-loop He
  recirculation), out-of-plane magnet
- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
  operating-edge questions
- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
- **Status**: in service

## Magnet

- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
  `field` qcodes Parameter.
- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
  floor.
- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output

  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).

  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,

  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads

  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.

  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.

  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).

  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the

  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

- **Device id**: `vti-02`

  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.

## Gate stack
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).

  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
  provided (below).

  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via

Aborted at 3 min (interrupted, gates parked at 0). Same map at **100 µV = 10 kΩ full scale** — the expert rule: lose low-R resolution (60 Ω = 0.6 % of range, readable per runs 0–3 at 0.4 %) rather than saturate. Everything else unchanged: TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] V 66 pts, BG slow [−1.3, +1.2] V 63 rows, fast_delay 1 s, leak guard on. Run-4 rate: 48–50 rows/min → 4158 pts ≈ 85 min + turnarounds. print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.02), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1)")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.02 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1, "gate-current nplci not reset to 1"

Vtg_vec = np.linspace(-0.3, 1.0, 66)    # fast, 20 mV
Vbg_vec = np.linspace(-1.3, 1.2, 63)    # slow, 40 mV

## Run 5 — 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`

Raw map (log R, TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] × BG slow [−1.3, +1.2], 20 × 40 mV, sr1 100 µV; run 4 was the same map aborted at 3 min when the ridge railed at 2 kΩ). **Read:** one dominant CNP ridge (A) running from (V_tg, V_bg) ≈ (+1.0, −1.3) to (−0.3, +0.45), plus a fainter **parallel** ridge (B) ≈ 0.19 V lower in V_tg — the second peak of runs 0–3. Ridge A's resistance is 240 Ω near D ≈ 0 and grows to ~2.4 kΩ at raw D ≈ +0.25 V/nm (saturating beyond), i.e. a D-tunable gap; **not a stacking read** (investigation Step 1 addendum: three candidate parents). """cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import sys, json, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5
g = fan_grids(f"data/{rid}"); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")
nB = calc_nD(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0] if len(ridgeB) else np.array([np.nan])
print(f"ridge B density offset relative to A: n_B = {np.nanmedian(nB):+.3f}e12 (std {np.nanstd(nB):.3f}), i.e. region B is {'hole' if np.nanmedian(nB)>0 else 'electron'}-doped vs A by {abs(np.nanmedian(nB)):.2f}e12")
# D = 0 line of region A: V_tg = (c_bg/c_tg) V_bg + V_tg0 where n=0 at ... use calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 4.5, 601); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (Vt >= -0.3) & (Vt <= 1.0) & (Vb >= -1.3) & (Vb <= 2.0)
print(f"D = 0 line (region A) realized n-window inside validators: {ns[ok].min():+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max():+.2f} e12; "
      f"CNP at (Vtg, Vbg) = ({calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[0]:+.3f}, {calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[1]:+.3f})")
# D range along ridge A
DA = calc_nD(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[1]
print(f"ridge A spans D = {DA.min():+.3f} .. {DA.max():+.3f} V/nm; peak R vs D: " +
      ", ".join(f"{d:+.2f}:{r:.0f}" for d, r in sorted(zip(np.round(DA, 2), ridgeA[:, 2]))[::6]))
json.dump({"run": rid, "ratio": ratio, "c_tg": c_tg, "c_bg": c_bg, "n_offset": n_offset, "D_offset": 0.0,
           "slope": cf[0], "intercept": cf[1], "window": "A |Vbg|<0.5", "nB_offset": float(np.nanmedian(nB))},
          open("hera_scratch/cal_run5.json", "w"), indent=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="log10 |Rxx| (Ohm)")
ax[0].plot(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], "c.", ms=3, label="ridge A pts"); ax[0].plot(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], "g.", ms=3, label="ridge B pts")
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()])
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cf, xx), xx, "w--", lw=1, label=f"A fit (op. window): slope {cf[0]:+.3f}")
if cfB_all is not None: ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cfB_all, xx), xx, "g--", lw=1, label=f"B fit: slope {cfB_all[0]:+.3f}")
ax[0].plot(Vt[ok], Vb[ok], "y:", lw=1.5, label="D = 0 (calibrated)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap — ridges + calibration")
# (n, D) projection
N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run{rid}.png", dpi=110); print("saved hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run5.png")

from hera.analysis import fan_grids, resistance_grids
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 5
g = fan_grids(f"data/{rid}"); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")
nB = calc_nD(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0] if len(ridgeB) else np.array([np.nan])
print(f"ridge B density offset relative to A: n_B = {np.nanmedian(nB):+.3f}e12 (std {np.nanstd(nB):.3f}), i.e. region B is {'hole' if np.nanmedian(nB)>0 else 'electron'}-doped vs A by {abs(np.nanmedian(nB)):.2f}e12")
# D = 0 line of region A: V_tg = (c_bg/c_tg) V_bg + V_tg0 where n=0 at ... use calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 4.5, 601); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (Vt >= -0.3) & (Vt <= 1.0) & (Vb >= -1.3) & (Vb <= 2.0)
print(f"D = 0 line (region A) realized n-window inside validators: {ns[ok].min():+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max():+.2f} e12; "
      f"CNP at (Vtg, Vbg) = ({calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[0]:+.3f}, {calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[1]:+.3f})")
# D range along ridge A
DA = calc_nD(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[1]
print(f"ridge A spans D = {DA.min():+.3f} .. {DA.max():+.3f} V/nm; peak R vs D: " +
      ", ".join(f"{d:+.2f}:{r:.0f}" for d, r in sorted(zip(np.round(DA, 2), ridgeA[:, 2]))[::6]))
json.dump({"run": rid, "ratio": ratio, "c_tg": c_tg, "c_bg": c_bg, "n_offset": n_offset, "D_offset": 0.0,
           "slope": cf[0], "intercept": cf[1], "window": "A |Vbg|<0.5", "nB_offset": float(np.nanmedian(nB))},
          open("hera_scratch/cal_run5.json", "w"), indent=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="log10 |Rxx| (Ohm)")
ax[0].plot(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], "c.", ms=3, label="ridge A pts"); ax[0].plot(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], "g.", ms=3, label="ridge B pts")
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()])
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cf, xx), xx, "w--", lw=1, label=f"A fit (op. window): slope {cf[0]:+.3f}")
if cfB_all is not None: ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cfB_all, xx), xx, "g--", lw=1, label=f"B fit: slope {cfB_all[0]:+.3f}")
ax[0].plot(Vt[ok], Vb[ok], "y:", lw=1.5, label="D = 0 (calibrated)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap — ridges + calibration")
# (n, D) projection
N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run{rid}.png", dpi=110); print("saved hera_scratch/cnp_cal_run5.png")

## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). The D = 0 line inside the validators spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹², so the electron side is the high-|n| side: spot at **n = +3.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.984, +1.166) V, 16 mV under the TG limit. **Feasibility (Step 2, model table):** F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB pair ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T (m* 0.028 / 0.061 mₑ), ABCA singleton 33.1 T (m* 0.074); the heavy-ABAB-vs-ABCA split is 7.5 T. Grid: uniform in B (blocking magnet) — 50 mT from 0 to 1 T (MR background only; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K kills m* = 0.06 below ~1.5 T), **10 mT from 1 to 10 T**; 921 points. Dwell: `delay = 0` — each `magnet.field` set blocks through the ramp plus the driver's 3 s settle = 10 τ at τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, i.e. the lock-in is at the settling floor at every point. Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).
====
# === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12 cm^-2, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm; (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}); '
              f'B 0 -> 10 T uniform-B (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.sweep(magnet.field, B_vec, delay=0)
# gates stay at the spot; field stays at 10 T (the hole-side spot check rides it down) — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f})")
====
## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

I_TRIP = 1e-9

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

## Lock-in channel / gain model

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.

### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
label mentions "current".

### `Channel` (dataclass)
`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.

### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.

---

## Fan re-forming and resistances

### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.

### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
`slow_param`.
- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.

### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
for Rxy/Hall.

### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
signed R grid, Ω).

---

## Shubnikov–de Haas

### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH

# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.

Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
label mentions "current".

### `Channel` (dataclass)
`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.

### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.

---

## Fan re-forming and resistances

### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.

### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
`slow_param`.
- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.

### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a

`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one

returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign

cell 12  [markdown]
============================================================
## Run 5 — 0 T gatemap (`gatemap`) → `cnp-and-dline-calibration`

Raw map (log R, TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] × BG slow [−1.3, +1.2], 20 × 40 mV, sr1 100 µV; run 4 was the same map aborted at 3 min when the ridge railed at 2 kΩ). **Read:** one dominant CNP ridge (A) running from (V_tg, V_bg) ≈ (+1.0, −1.3) to (−0.3, +0.45), plus a fainter **parallel** ridge (B) ≈ 0.19 V lower in V_tg — the second peak of runs 0–3. Ridge A's resistance is 240 Ω near D ≈ 0 and grows to ~2.4 kΩ at raw D ≈ +0.25 V/nm (saturating beyond), i.e. a D-tunable gap; **not a stacking read** (investigation Step 1 addendum: three candidate parents). Fits (ridge position = V_tg vs V_bg rows, so −slope = c_bg/c_tg): ridge A in the operating window |V_bg| < 0.5: slope −0.773 (rms 19 mV); high-D rows: −0.763 (rms 6 mV); ridge B: −0.69 (8 rows, rms 13 mV). **Calibration:** ratio c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data-calibrated; prior 0.864, −11 % — plausible hBN-thickness error, not a transposition); c_tg anchored at the 9.5 nm prior (absolute scale = geometry prior, pending a lever-arm check); n_offset = −0.089×10¹²; **D_offset from the R_CNP(D) symmetry** (vertex of the ridge-A resistance minimum, ≈ +0.012 raw) — the one feature that physically locates D = 0. """SdH spot checks (runs 6, 7): raw R(B), background-removed oscillatory part vs 1/B, FFT in 1/B, sdh_onset read.
Usage: menv python hera_scratch/spot_analysis.py"""
import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, SdhOnsetError, luttinger_frequency

def load(rid):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    o = np.argsort(B)
    return r, B[o], R[o], I[o], r.col("T_sample")[o]

runs = {6: ("electron n=+3.2e12", 3.2), 7: ("hole n=-1.2e12", -1.2)}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 11))
for k, (rid, (lab, n12)) in enumerate(runs.items()):
    r, B, R, I, T = load(rid)
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16)
    print(f"\n=== run {rid} ({lab}) === {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.2f}..{B.max():.2f} T; R {R.min():.1f}..{R.max():.1f} Ohm; "
          f"I {I.min()*1e9:.2f}..{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; T {T.min():.3f}..{T.max():.3f} K; F_L(full n, 4-fold) = {FL:.1f} T")
    ax[0, k].plot(B, R, lw=0.8); ax[0, k].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[0, k].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax[0, k].set_title(f"run {rid} — {lab} — raw")
    # oscillatory part: poly background in B over B >= 1 T
    m = B >= 1.0
    cf = np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5); dR = R[m] - np.polyval(cf, B[m])
    ax[1, k].plot(1 / B[m], dR, lw=0.8); ax[1, k].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax[1, k].set_ylabel("dRxx (Ohm)"); ax[1, k].set_title("bg-removed (deg-5 in B), B >= 1 T")
    for b_lo in (1.0, 2.0, 3.0):
        try:
            f, spec = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(b_lo, B.max()), nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False)
            sp = spec[0]; sel = f > 2
            pk = f[sel][np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]]
            print(f"  FFT window [{b_lo}, {B.max():.1f}] T: top peaks at F = {np.round(np.sort(pk), 1)} T  (dF ~ {1/(1/b_lo - 1/B.max()):.1f} T)")
            if b_lo == 2.0: ax[2, k].plot(f, sp / sp[sel].max(), lw=1, label=f"[{b_lo},{B.max():.0f}] T")
            if b_lo == 1.0: ax[2, k].plot(f, sp / sp[sel].max(), lw=0.7, alpha=0.6, label=f"[{b_lo},{B.max():.0f}] T")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  FFT [{b_lo}, ..] failed: {e}")
    ax[2, k].axvline(FL, color="r", ls="--", lw=1, label=f"F_L = {FL:.1f} T (n/4 deg)")
    ax[2, k].axvline(FL / 2, color="orange", ls=":", lw=1, label="F_L/2")
    ax[2, k].set_xlim(0, 60); ax[2, k].set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax[2, k].set_ylabel("FFT amp (norm)"); ax[2, k].legend(fontsize=7)
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=0.5, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print(f"  sdh_onset: {e}")
    # local extrema count in dR above 3 T as a crude tone check
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    mm = B[m] >= 3
    pks, _ = find_peaks(dR[mm], prominence=np.std(dR[mm]) * 0.5)
    print(f"  dR maxima above 3 T: {len(pks)}; positions (T): {np.round(B[m][mm][pks], 2)}")
    print(f"  1/B of maxima: {np.round(1/B[m][mm][pks], 4)}; diffs: {np.round(np.diff(1/B[m][mm][pks]), 4)}")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/spot_runs67.png", dpi=110); print("\nsaved hera_scratch/spot_runs67.png")

# === Gate C — liveness + gross gate safety: gate-current-sanity-check (first-session branch) ===
# Four legs, each gate 0 -> each card limit with the other parked at 0, 101 pts, delay 1 s,
# nplci=10 on the gate-current channels (pA floor). Lock-in X on sr1 (B_1-B_2) + sr0 (drain)
# answer "is the device alive on the provided contacts"; gate currents answer "is it safe".
# Automatic abort: |I_gate| > 1 nA on either Keithley trips the sweep (no operator eyes in E1).
from sharpelab_nb.autorange import autorange_sr830s

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0 = T_sample(); _B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (expect 1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (expect |B|<0.02), "
      f"V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.3f}, V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.3f}, V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (expect 0)")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5, f"T_sample {_T0} K off base"
assert abs(_B0) < 0.02, f"magnet not at zero: {_B0} T"
assert abs(k_si()) < 0.01, "Si gate not at 0"

legs = [(k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN), (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN)]
n_pts, delay = 101, 1.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9   # A — hard abort threshold on either gate current

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels (reset at the end if no leg tripped)
k_tg.nplci(10); k_bg.nplci(10)

# sr1 sensitivity sized for an unknown Rxx: 500 uV = 50 kOhm full scale at I_bias = 10 nA
# (drive 1 V / 100 MOhm, as the operator set it); autorange hook tracks from there.
sr1.sensitivity(500e-6)
print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V @ {sr1.frequency()} Hz -> I_bias ~ {sr1.amplitude()/100e6*1e9:.1f} nA; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s")

tripped = []
for gate, v_end in legs:
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    mc = dict(meas_config); mc["comments"] = f"gate-current-sanity-check: {gate.name} 0 -> {v_end:+g} V, other gate 0, Si 0, B 0"
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}; leg: 0 -> {v_end:+g} V (card limit); {other.name} parked 0; Vsi = 0; B = 0')
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    xp = gate.volt
    # row layout: [time, setpoint, other.volt, gate.curr, other.curr, T_sample, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
    s.fp(other.volt).fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr).fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr); s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, sr1.X); s.plot(xp, sr0.X)
    s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, (sr0, [sr1]))

    def leak_guard(station, data, _gate=gate):
        i_g, i_o = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
        if i_g > I_TRIP or i_o > I_TRIP:
            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

if tripped:
    print("STOP — a leg tripped the leakage guard; nplci left at 10, gates parked at 0:", tripped)
else:
    k_tg.nplci(1); k_bg.nplci(1)
    print("all four legs ran without a leakage trip; nplci reset to 1")
    print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals, "| k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)

    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}; leg: 0 -> {v_end:+g} V (card limit); {other.name} parked 0; Vsi = 0; B = 0')
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    xp = gate.volt
    # row layout: [time, setpoint, other.volt, gate.curr, other.curr, T_sample, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
    s.fp(other.volt).fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr).fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr); s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, sr1.X); s.plot(xp, sr0.X)
    s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, (sr0, [sr1]))

    def leak_guard(station, data, _gate=gate):
        i_g, i_o = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
        if i_g > I_TRIP or i_o > I_TRIP:
            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

if tripped:
    print("STOP — a leg tripped the leakage guard; nplci left at 10, gates parked at 0:", tripped)
else:
    k_tg.nplci(1); k_bg.nplci(1)
    print("all four legs ran without a leakage trip; nplci reset to 1")
    print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals, "| k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 10 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 600000ms are capped to 600000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# vti-02 — stacking-order plan (HERA, 2026-08-23 pickup)

Goal: ABAB vs ABCA vs ABCB on the one wired pair (sr1 = B_1–B_2, source T_0, drain B_3), evidence-cited, or a calibrated "cannot tell".

## Discriminants (what each stacking predicts, D = 0)
- **ABAB (Bernal)**: two bilayer-like bands (light + heavy) → **two SdH fundamentals** whose frequencies sum to F_L = n·h/4e; Landau fan shows two interpenetrating ladders with **LL crossings**; 16-fold zero-energy LL → first strong gap |ν| = 8 (4-fold splittings weaker); CNP gap opens with |D| symmetrically.
- **ABCA (rhombohedral)**: single flat band → **one SdH fundamental at F_L** (plus harmonics only); a single clean ladder, gaps at |ν| = 8, 12, 16, … no crossings at D = 0; strong D-tunable CNP gap; strong interaction physics near CNP.
- **ABCB (mixed)**: no inversion symmetry → intrinsic gap at D = 0 (R_CNP(D) minimum displaced or absent), Dirac-like + heavy band mix; asymmetric ladder.

## Steps
1. ✅ Gate C liveness (runs 0–3): alive, no leakage (|I| ≲ 100 pA transients only), peaks ≤ 330 Ω at D≈0.
2. ✅ 0 T gatemap (run 5; run 4 railed) → calibration: c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 9.5 nm prior, n_offset −0.089e12, D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) vertex). D = 0 line inside the box: n = −1.27 … +3.27e12. Second parallel ridge B (mosaic, +0.43e12) is a confound to keep in mind.
3. ✅ SdH spot checks (run 6 electron n=+3.2e12; run 7 hole n=−1.2e12): SdH resolvable from ~1.5 T at base T. Run 6: fundamentals ≈ 7.2 T and ≈ 30 T (+ harmonics) — two-band-like; sum ≈ 37 T vs F_L 33.1 T → absolute n scale (prior) likely ~10 % low, or the 30 T tone is partly harmonic. Run 7: multi-tone (6.8, 12.3 ≈ F_L, 3.5, 15.8 T) — near-CNP, not decisive.
4. **▶ Fan 1 — coarse full-window D = 0 Landau fan** (`landau-fan`): B slow 0.4 → 10 T in 0.2 T (49 rows), fast = D = 0 line n −1.25 … +3.25e12 in 0.03e12 (151 pts, both carrier signs). Establishes: the ν-ladder (which |ν| gaps, crossings or not), F(n) per band from per-column FFT (slope of F vs n = absolute-n calibration = the lever-arm check), electron/hole asymmetry. Ends at 10 T with gates parked at 0. ~4 h.
5. **Fan 2 — targeted down-fan** (10 → ~1 T, direction alternated per the rig card): after Fan 1, zoom where the discriminant lives — finer B (0.1 T) over the crossing/gap window, or a D ≠ 0 fan if the D = 0 read is ambiguous (ABCA vs ABAB differ strongly in how the ladder responds to D). Priced after Fan 1.
6. Optional: T-dependence of a chosen gap (LK mass) only if Fans 1–2 leave the call weak and time allows (elevated-T rig facts read first).
7. Call in ana (output contract), then `return-to-initial` close-out on operator ask.

## What would change my mind
- Fan 1 shows a **single** clean ladder with F(n) = F_L for all n → ABCA-leaning; then Fan 2 tests D-dependence of the gap sequence.
- Fan 1 shows **two** ladders/crossings and two F(n) branches summing to F_L → ABAB-leaning; Fan 2 zooms crossings (their B positions vs n are quantitative).
- R_CNP(D) minimum not at the symmetry point / ladder asymmetric between ±n at D = 0 → ABCB in play.
- Rails at ν = 0 near n = 0 at high B are expected (accept); rails elsewhere → re-run row window at 200 µV.
- Region B (mosaic) tones at ×1.13 density would appear as faint replica lines — do not count them as bands.

from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_line = np.round(np.arange(-1.25, 3.25 + 1e-9, 0.03), 4)          # 1e12 cm^-2, 151 pts, both carrier signs

Vtg_line, Vbg_line = calc_gate_voltages(n_line, np.full_like(n_line, D_line), CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
Vtg_line, Vbg_line = np.asarray(Vtg_line), np.asarray(Vbg_line)

        station.interrupt_requested = True

    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)

## HERA — Fan 1: D = 0 Landau fan, full n-window, both carrier signs (`landau-fan`, plan step 4)

**Why now.** The spot checks (runs 6, 7 — analysis in ana) show SdH resolvable from ≈ 1.5 T at base T: run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) carries two fundamentals, ≈ 7.2 T and ≈ 30 T with harmonics (a two-band-like spectrum; their sum ≈ 37 T vs F_L = 33.1 T means the absolute n-scale — still the 9.5 nm prior — is likely ~10 % low, or the 30 T tone is partly harmonic); run 7 (hole, n = −1.2×10¹²) is multi-tone near the CNP. Neither is a stacking read: that needs the **ν-ladder** (which |ν| gaps, crossings or a single clean ladder) and **F(n) per band** (slope = absolute-n calibration = the lever-arm check). Both come from one fan.

**Design.** Slow axis B 0.4 → 10 T in 0.2 T (49 rows, starts where the magnet sits, ends at 10 T so Fan 2 rides down — no re-traverse). Fast axis the run-5 D = 0 line, n = −1.25 … +3.25×10¹² in 0.03×10¹² (151 pts, co-swept V_tg/V_bg via `multimegasweep`; both gates inside the validators, asserted in-cell). Full coverage of the D = 0 window inside the box — nothing excluded; hole side is TG-limited at −1.27. sr1 fixed at 100 µV (10 kΩ FS): spot checks peaked at 590 Ω at 10 T; only ν = 0 near n = 0 at high B should exceed FS (rail = gap, accepted). fast_delay 1 s / slow_delay 3 s as run 5 (1.17 s/pt measured). Leak guard 1 nA on both gates. Gates park at 0 at the end; field left at 10 T.

**Price.** Bare 9.6 T traverse 70 min + 49 rows × (151 × 1.17 s + settle + flyback ≈ 185 s) ≈ 2.5 h → 3.7 h; realistic 4 h.

**Checkpoints.** (1) First two rows (~12 min): rail? leakage? R(n) shape vs run 5 at low B. (2) Hourly: re-form the partial fan (`fan_grids`), look for the ladder / crossings; abort if the channel rails broadly or the map is featureless above 3 T (then the read is resolution-limited and Fan 2 is redesigned rather than paid for).
